title: Arabic for Non-Arabic Speakers – Level 03
overview: This pre-intermediate Arabic language course develops learners' ability to communicate beyond routine exchanges in everyday, social and workplace contexts. Building on Levels 01 and 02, participants learn to connect ideas, recount experiences, describe plans, express opinions and understand the main points of clear spoken and written Arabic. Lessons integrate Modern Standard Arabic for literacy and structured communication with practical spoken expressions, while distinguishing register and common regional usage where relevant. The emphasis is on meaningful interaction, accuracy, listening confidence and increasingly independent language use.
audience: Non-Arabic-speaking learners who have completed Level 02 or have equivalent elementary proficiency.
Expatriate residents seeking more confident Arabic communication in community and social settings.
Customer-facing, administrative and operational employees communicating with Arabic-speaking colleagues or clients.
Learners preparing to progress toward intermediate Arabic study and more sustained conversations.
methodology: Communicative instructor-led lessons; guided conversations and role plays; short authentic listening and reading materials; structured grammar practice; pronunciation and vocabulary workshops; paired information-gap tasks; practical writing assignments; contextualized cultural scenarios; formative quizzes; individual feedback; and an integrated end-of-course speaking, listening, reading and writing assessment.
competencies: Participating in connected conversations on familiar personal, community and work-related topics.
Understanding the main points and relevant details in clear, moderately paced Arabic speech.
Describing experiences, plans, preferences and reasons using connected sentences.
Reading short practical texts and identifying main ideas, supporting information and intended meaning.
Writing coherent messages and short paragraphs with appropriate sequencing and basic accuracy.
Selecting suitable vocabulary, polite expressions and formal or informal registers for the context.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Sustain conversations through follow-up questions, clarification and appropriate responses.
Describe past experiences, current situations and future plans in logically connected language.
Express preferences, comparisons, opinions and simple reasons with growing fluency.
Understand the gist and key details of everyday announcements, conversations and short recordings.
Read and interpret notices, messages, short articles and workplace-related texts.
Write organized messages, descriptions and short narratives using common linking expressions.
Use frequent verb forms, sentence patterns and agreement rules more accurately.
Apply culturally appropriate greetings, requests, apologies and interaction strategies.
